title: You Are Not Alone. Everyone Else Is Home Too.
desc:
You are not alone. Everyone else is home too, scrolling the same few party stories and thinking the same thing about you.

Saturday, 9 PM. Dave follows a hundred people and nine of them posted parties. So where are the other ninety-one? A national time-use survey, eleven Cornell studies and the World Health Organization all point to the same answer, and it ends with one message.

⏱ Chapters
0:00 Everyone is out except Dave
0:08 Where are the other 91?
0:16 What people really do on weekends
0:26 Why everyone seems out
0:42 One in six
0:48 To them, Dave is out
0:54 Text one

Sources:
- Deri, Davidai & Gilovich (2017), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, "Home alone": in 11 studies (3,293 people), most believed others lead richer social lives, because socialites come to mind first
- U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey 2025: on weekends, 55 minutes a day socialising and 3.3 hours watching TV
- WHO Commission on Social Connection (2025): 1 in 6 people worldwide is affected by loneliness
- Liu, Rim, Min & Min (2022), Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, "The surprise of reaching out": people underestimate how much others appreciate hearing from them

Try it tonight: send one message to one person you haven't talked to in a while. "What are you up to?" is enough.

If loneliness feels heavy or lasts a long time, talking to a doctor or a local support line is a good next step.

New videos every week: the strange science behind the things you worry about.
